vignette: Raj is a 32-year-old South Asian man who works as a housekeeper in the bustling city of San Francisco. He and his wife, Priya, have been married for eight years, and they live together in a modest apartment near their work. Raj's life took an unexpected turn about six months ago when he was mugged outside a building where he had just completed cleaning. On that fateful evening, Raj left the building at 10 PM after finishing his shift. As he walked towards his car parked on the street, a masked individual emerged from the shadows and demanded his wallet. Despite Raj's compliance, the assailant became violent, punching him in the face and stealing not only his wallet but also his phone and keys. The attack was swift but left Raj shaken to his core. Since that night, Raj experiences intense flashbacks whenever he hears footsteps behind him or sees a shadowy figure on the street. He relives the fear and pain of that moment vividly, often feeling as though the attacker is still present in these scenarios. These intrusive thoughts have made it difficult for him to walk alone at night, which has significantly impacted his routine of taking evening walks with Priya. Raj's work performance has also been affected. He finds himself constantly on edge while cleaning rooms and apartments, particularly when he hears unexpected noises or notices something out of place. The anxiety often manifests as a racing heart and sweaty palms, making it hard for him to concentrate. His supervisor has noticed Raj's increasing difficulty in handling simple tasks that used to be second nature. The mugging has also strained his relationship with Priya. Raj is often irritable and short-tempered, which he finds frustrating because he doesn't mean to lash out at her. He feels guilty for being distant and less affectionate than before. They have had several conversations about how the trauma has changed him, but he struggles to express what he's going through. Raj also experiences severe nightmares, reliving the mugging multiple times a week. In these dreams, the attacker is more aggressive and threatening, leaving Raj drenched in sweat and struggling to calm down before he can fall back asleep. These disturbances disrupt his sleep patterns, leading to exhaustion during the day and further affecting his mood and overall functioning. One of the most distressing aspects for Raj is the sense of vulnerability that lingers from the attack. He avoids going out alone at night and sometimes even hesitates to leave the apartment unless absolutely necessary. The fear of being attacked again is omnipresent, and he has become hypervigilant in public spaces, constantly scanning his surroundings. Despite these challenges, Raj remains committed to his work and tries to maintain a normal routine with Priya. He talks about feeling like a burden on her at times but also values the support she provides. Recently, he started taking short breaks during his shifts to practice deep breathing exercises that help him manage some of his anxiety symptoms. Raj's story is one of resilience in the face of trauma. Although he continues to grapple with flashbacks, hypervigilance, and nightmares, he remains dedicated to finding ways to cope and regain a sense of control over his life. The ongoing support from Priya has been crucial in helping him navigate through this difficult period.
